top.line: RiskMandate's partner programme: products that see agents at work gain what their logs cannot tell them.
top.para: Gateways, identity, observability and cost tools see agents but not what each is for. A behaviour policy writes it down and turns measurements into judgements. Three ways in: integration, referral and co-sell. RiskMandate gives the mandate API, templates, co-branding and case studies; partners give evidence, unowned agents and a route to customers. Terms are proposals.

in-short.line: Many products see agents; none sees what each is for; three ways to work together.
in-short.para: The first case study is cost; shares and prices are proposals.

why.line: RiskMandate uses what the customer already has and adds the missing piece: the mandate.
why.para: Seen already with WSO2's gateway interceptor and the cost case study; a programme makes it repeatable.

tiers.line: Integration partners return evidence through the mandate API; referral and co-sell partners share customers.
tiers.para: Referral shares and co-sell pricing are proposed, not published.

gives.line: RiskMandate gives the API, templates, co-branding and joint case studies; partners give evidence and reach.
gives.para: Evidence turns written rows into measured ones and can be priced like insurance.

gtm.line: A design partner, a joint report, a published case study and a packaged offer.
gtm.para: Each joint offer opens with one yes-or-no question for the customer.

looking.line: Cost and FinOps tools, AI gateways, agent identity, observability, sandboxes, insurers and brokers.
looking.para: The cost case study shows what working together looks like.

limits.line: The programme is new; no partner has signed; terms are proposals.
limits.para: The mandate API uses the policy model already published.

sources.line: The editor's conversation of 3 November 2026 and the cost vault.
